keyFindings.summary: BRAT data.json uses pluginList, pluginSubListFrozenVersion, themesList, scalar booleans/string settings, and deprecated token compatibility fields.
pluginSubListFrozenVersion stores repo plus version and optional token/tokenName/isIncompatible; pluginList remains the membership list.
themesList entries store repo and the downloaded CSS checksum as lastUpdate.
Current plugin installation is release-asset-first and requires a valid release manifest.
Pinned installs use releases/tags; latest installs enumerate releases and apply semantic-version/date ordering.
Plugin assets are written under .obsidian/plugins/{manifest.id}; enableAfterInstall calls Obsidian enablePluginAndSave.
Pinned entries are skipped by ordinary update cycles.
Theme installation prefers theme-beta.css, writes theme.css plus manifest.json, selects the theme, and tracks the CSS checksum.
BRAT registers current command-palette entries through PluginCommands.bratCommands.
Current source exposes one add-plugin flow with or without a release version; protocol parameters may prefill repo and version.
BRAT registers its protocol handler and schedules plugin/theme update work after layout readiness.
Installed files, enabled plugin state, and BRAT repository registration are independent file-layer states.
sources: inference: BetaPlugins install/enable flow plus settings persistence

keyFindings.summary: Private repositories require read-capable tokens resolved through SecretStorage token names; data.json alone cannot provision the secret.
Failure branches include missing releases/assets, malformed manifests, compatibility/mobile gates, authentication/rate limits, and missing theme files.
Removing tracked plugins/themes removes registration only; installed files remain.
BRAT protocol opens plugin/theme add flows but does not directly enable or disable plugins.
